roster.robots_disclosed: Dozens of Walker S1 robots; one Walker S2 described subsequently
roster.note: Zeekr is consolidated to its parent Geely Holding. The March source was opened: it reports actual sorting, heavy-workpiece handling and precision assembly across production areas at the named Zeekr factory, rather than merely a training-centre deployment or future plan. Counted as an in-factory pilot under R2 despite its practical-training label; no production volumes or intervention rates disclosed. Walker S2 parts handling is corroborative. Event 178 combines a July 2025 capability announcement with a March 2026 factory report; its July date is not used to backdate the later corroboration. No different-job deployment elsewhere established in the ledger claims.

roster.ended: 2026-10-07-forbes-bmw-figure-scope — No Figure robots currently operating at BMW; the June 2026 return was a non-production test that also ended. The earlier Figure 02 production pilot was retired in event 2025-11-19-figure-02-bmw-production-run-r2. Retained cumulatively under R5.
roster.note: Earliest explicit live-production evidence is the April 2025 Fortune report: one robot picking parts from a logistics container and loading a body-shop welding fixture, after non-production-only testing until March. Reject the November 2024 fleet claim as a production start. Later sources disclose two robots, only one working at a time. 90,000+ parts, 1,250+ runtime hours and 30,000+ vehicles; zero-intervention figures were targets, not achieved measurements. Figure 02 also does a different job, parcel barcode orientation, at the vendor evaluation site in event 177; redeployed means different job elsewhere, not necessarily another qualifying customer.

Commercial tote handling between AMRs, conveyor and floor locations at Flowery Branch. More than 100,000 totes; exact fleet size undisclosed, so the 2–5 estimate is not treated as a disclosed count. Use the event published date, not the older deployment date or the original linked announcement date. A distinct job elsewhere is bearing-basket handling at Schaeffler. Task accuracy of approximately 98% is not an intervention rate.

High-voltage battery-connector insertion on the Zhongzhou production line. Opened SCMP/Yahoo source explicitly identifies Spirit AI as the robot builder, not just a model supplier. Claimed 99% task success and triple human daily workload; no achieved intervention rate, fleet size or different-job deployment disclosed.

One Digit moves 25-pound bearing-component baskets from stamping press to washing machine, eight hours daily in two four-hour shifts. The opened report describes automated work but no measured interventions or independent examination of the control system. Different job elsewhere: tote handling at GXO.

Tablet loading/unloading at MMIT test stations on a live mass-production line. Four robots in April, eight in June. April eight-hour shift, 18–20 seconds per operation and up to 310 units/hour; June six-day deployment reported 64+ operating hours, 64,828 tasks and 17,625 units. Success percentages and minimal-human-intervention wording do not disclose an intervention rate. Humans and maintenance team remain present; no teleoperation of the counted work is stated. Multiple workflows here are not a different job elsewhere.

Parcel picking and label-up reorientation at the Longgang logistics centre. R1 explicitly admits column-based humanoids; not reclassified as a conventional fixed-arm cell. Opened Economic Observer source describes six robots during a 1 a.m. shift and reports human troubleshooting of disconnects/stoppages and supervision, providing independent reporting on interventions, though no numerical rate. Stable 1,200 parcels/hour by end-May. Six is the disclosed local fleet, not a China Post-wide total. Use the event publication date of June 2, not the retrospective November arrival or May 20 secondary source. The other named logistics operator in the full source is not added from a bare customer-list mention.

Autonomous heavy-material-bin transport between module and battery-pack stations at Ningde; source explicitly says without remote control. Claimed 7×24 operation for three months after March acceptance, but first qualifying event published June 24. Separate vendor from Spirit AI, same parent customer CATL. No fleet size or intervention rate disclosed.
